title: Journalists protest at Delhi police station over alleged sexual harassment
seoTitle: Delhi journalists' protest over police harassment

tea.why: Three women journalists say police officers sexually harassed them while they covered the Oct 3 anti-CEC protest at Jantar Mantar.
tea.want: An FIR against the accused officers, release of CCTV footage and an impartial investigation.
tea.changed: Oct 5: police detained 17 protesters, including one complainant, and registered an FIR against them.

summary: Independent journalists, YouTubers and activists have protested outside Delhi's Parliament Street police station since October 3, after three women journalists alleged that police officers sexually harassed them while they were covering the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner at Jantar Mantar. One complainant said a senior officer pushed and assaulted her when she asked why no women police were present during detentions. Delhi Police said the complaints, and the women's medical examinations, were forwarded to the Crime Branch for an impartial inquiry, but no FIR had been registered on them. On October 5, after protesters spent a second night outside the station, police detained about 17 people, including one of the complainants, and registered an FIR against them, according to The Hindu. The same day the accused officer was among 12 officers promoted to Additional DCP; senior officers called it a routine order.
demands: Register an FIR against the accused officers
Release CCTV footage of the incident
response: Delhi Police forwarded the complaints to the Crime Branch for an impartial inquiry, detained about 17 protesters on Oct 5 and registered an FIR against them; senior officers said the accused officer's promotion was routine.
